skill.name: MCP Integration
skill.description: Comprehensive guidance for integrating Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers into Claude Code plugins. Covers stdio, SSE, HTTP, and WebSocket server types, .mcp.json configuration, authentication patterns, and using MCP tools in commands and agents.
skill.summary: Configure and integrate MCP servers into Claude Code plugins for external tools and services.
skill.author: anthropics

security_audit.summary: This is an official Anthropic documentation skill that teaches how to configure Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers in Claude Code plugins. All 158 static findings were adjudicated as false positives: they are Markdown code fences flagged as backtick execution, documentation and example URLs flagged as hardcoded URLs, ${ENV_VAR} placeholders (the recommended secure secret pattern) flagged as credential access, and illustrative bash snippets inside fenced code blocks. The skill contains no executable scripts and performs no network, filesystem, or command actions of its own. No semantic or intent-level issues (prompt injection, data exfiltration, social engineering) were found.

remediation.issue: Example configuration files use example.com placeholder URLs and ${ENV_VAR} secret references.
remediation.suggestion: No change required. These are intentional teaching placeholders and the correct secure pattern; keep referencing secrets via environment variables rather than hardcoding them.

static_findings.snippet: Connect to RESTful MCP servers via standard HTTP requests. Best for token-based auth and stateless i
Use `/mcp` command to see all servers including plugin-provided ones.
- **`references/server-types.md`** - Deep dive on each server type
- **`references/tool-usage.md`** - Using MCP tools in commands and agents
2. Create `.mcp.json` at plugin root with configuration
- Claude Code spawns and manages the process

content.user_title: Integrate MCP Servers Into Claude Code Plugins
content.value_statement: Connecting external tools and services to Claude Code plugins requires precise MCP configuration that is easy to get wrong. This skill provides ready-to-use patterns for every server type, authentication method, and tool-usage scenario so integrations work on the first try.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to create and structure .mcp.json configuration at the plugin root.
Documents all MCP server types: stdio, SSE, HTTP, and WebSocket, with example configs.
Covers authentication patterns including OAuth, token-based auth, and dynamic headers.
Shows how MCP tools are named and invoked from commands and agents.
Provides secure secret handling using environment variable references rather than hardcoded values.
Includes troubleshooting steps using the /mcp command and claude --debug logs.
limitations: This is a documentation skill; it provides guidance and examples but does not run or deploy MCP servers.
It does not supply the actual MCP server implementations you connect to.
Authentication credentials and server endpoints must be provided by the user.
Behavior depends on the Claude Code plugin system and current MCP specification.

output_examples.input: Add an MCP server to my plugin using .mcp.json.
output_examples.output: Guidance to create a .mcp.json file at the plugin root, with a server entry that specifies the server type, connection details, and any required environment variable references, plus steps to verify it with the /mcp command.

output_examples.input: Set up OAuth authentication for my SSE server.
output_examples.output: An explanation of the OAuth flow for hosted MCP servers, how to store tokens in environment variables, and how to reference them safely from the configuration without committing secrets.

best_practices: Reference secrets through environment variables such as ${API_KEY} instead of hardcoding them in configuration files.
Use HTTPS endpoints for remote servers and add .env files to .gitignore so credentials stay out of source control.
Verify each server with the /mcp command and check claude --debug logs before relying on the integration.
anti_patterns: Do not commit real API keys, tokens, or database passwords into .mcp.json or the plugin repository.
Do not use plain HTTP for remote MCP servers when HTTPS is available.
Do not skip verifying that the server appears in the /mcp output before using its tools.

faq.question: What is .mcp.json and where does it go?
faq.answer: It is the configuration file that declares MCP servers for a plugin. Place it at the plugin root so Claude Code can discover and load the servers.

faq.question: Which MCP server type should I use?
faq.answer: Use stdio for local processes, SSE or HTTP for hosted remote services, and WebSocket for bidirectional streaming. The reference docs describe the tradeoffs of each.

faq.question: How do I keep credentials secure?
faq.answer: Reference secrets through environment variables and never hardcode them. Store them outside the repository, for example in a .env file that is added to .gitignore.

faq.question: How are MCP tools named?
faq.answer: Tools follow the format mcp__plugin_<plugin-name>_<server-name>__<tool-name>, so you can reference a specific tool from a specific server.

faq.question: How do I verify my MCP server is connected?
faq.answer: Run the /mcp command to list available servers and tools, and review claude --debug logs if a server does not appear.

faq.question: Does this skill run the MCP servers for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides configuration guidance and examples. You supply the server implementations and credentials, and Claude Code manages the connections.
